clue.text: Make waves, as rough sea may

definitions.meaning: to cause trouble or disturb a settled situation
literally, a rough sea tips a vessel from side to side

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for stirring up trouble comes from a rocking vessel, and a heavy swell literally does that to a craft.

clue.text: They observed an enormous bird

definitions.meaning: the Royal Observer Corps, a British civilian body that watched for aircraft
the giant bird of Arabian legend, as in Sinbad's tales

explanation.definitionFit: The aircraft-spotting Royal Observer Corps went by its initials, and the legendary giant bird of the Arabian Nights shares that spelling.

clue.text: Scoundrels start to employ bad language

parts.note: curs are contemptible men, scoundrels

indicators.note: start to takes only the opening letter of employ

explanation.surface: Villains begin to use foul words.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse is an oath or swear word, foul speech.

clue.text: One acting legally for another, as set out in actual case

indicators.note: in means the reordered letters go inside the word for actual

parts.note: true means actual, the real case

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer represents someone, as the facts of a real case show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' reads as a legal matter in the surface, but here it describes the true word as the casing round the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee holds and manages property on behalf of beneficiaries under law.

clue.text: Trip over cross dog raised commotion

indicators.note: over means the turned-round commotion is draped around the cross and dog
raised in a down clue means the commotion word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: noise is a din, a commotion
X is the shape of a cross
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over an angry dog and causes an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' suits a down clue: the turned commotion sits around the cross and dog in the column. 'Trip' looks like a stumble but means an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion is an outing or short journey.

clue.text: Once at sea, crossing a body of water

indicators.note: crossing means the jumbled letters span either side of the a
at sea means confused, so the letters of once are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship once at sea crosses a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns ONCE into OCEN, and 'crossing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is one of the great expanses of salt water on Earth.

clue.text: Beam at stern matrons misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving means the letters of matrons act out of order

explanation.surface: Unruly matrons give a severe look.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a crosswise timber forming the back of a vessel's hull.

clue.text: Set a limit to EC policy

definitions.meaning: to put a ceiling on something
the European Community's Common Agricultural Policy, known by its initials

explanation.definitionFit: A ceiling put on spending is a cap, and the Common Agricultural Policy was the EC's farm subsidy scheme, abbreviated by its initials.

clue.text: Facility at ski resort for the upwardly mobile

definitions.text: Facility at ski resort for the upwardly mobile

parts.words: Facility at ski resort for the upwardly mobile
parts.note: upwardly mobile usually means socially ambitious, but here the people literally travel up the slope on a cable-borne seat

explanation.definitionFit: Skiers ride seats hung from a moving cable to the top of the slope.

clue.text: Main link opened by US in 1914

definitions.text: Main link opened by US in 1914

parts.words: Main link opened by US in 1914
parts.note: main is the sea; the waterway the United States opened in 1914 joins two oceans across Central America

explanation.definitionFit: The canal across the isthmus in Central America links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, opened under US control in 1914.

clue.text: Relative's put on almost two flipping stone

indicators.note: put on means the relative is placed after the other piece in an across answer
flipping turns the shortened word for a pair over so it reads backwards
almost means the word for a pair loses its final letter

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two of something
an uncle is a relative; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A family member is pushed onto a pair of things being tossed over a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' looks like the thing being flipped, but it is the definition: a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a precious red stone, a garnet cut with a rounded top.

clue.text: Turkish leader elected for second term

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman Turkish commander or chief
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A Turkish politician is voted into office for another stint.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a second time, or for a further spell, is doing it once more.

clue.text: Wrestle with complications, and become heated

indicators.note: with complications means the letters of the word are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Grappling with a knotty problem makes someone hot under the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: To swelter is to be oppressively hot and sweaty.

clue.text: After herbal remedies. I am taking dope

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the herbal remedies

parts.note: simples are medicines made from a single herb
I'm on, as in I am taking a medicine

explanation.surface: Someone on herbal cures admits to using drugs too.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMPLES for herbal medicines is old usage. The definition 'dope' is the slang for a fool, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme simpleton is a byword for a fool, which is what dope means here.

clue.text: Patent medicine is in no way unusual

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rum is an old British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A claim that an over-the-counter remedy is perfectly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' just links the definition to the wordplay. RUM for 'odd' is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy sold on the strength of its secret recipe, the classic patent medicine.

clue.text: Brilliant solver of clues used by Telegraph

definitions.meaning: Inspector ..., Colin Dexter's crossword-loving Oxford detective
the dot-and-dash code once tapped out on telegraph lines

explanation.definitionFit: Dexter's detective is famous both for cracking cases and for cryptic crosswords, and the code of dots and dashes bears the same inventor's name.

clue.text: Organise deliveries in deceitful practice

definitions.meaning: to operate a delivery route, making the rounds

explanation.definitionFit: Running a round is managing a delivery route, and being given evasive treatment is getting messed about.

clue.text: As a consequence of backing murderer, doctor's unable to sleep

parts.note: in can mean owing to, as in the phrase in consequence of

indicators.note: backing turns the murderer and the doctor's round so the pair read backwards

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
MO is a medical officer, a doctor; the 's is kept as S

explanation.surface: A doctor loses sleep after supporting a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns CAIN plus MOS into SOMNIAC. The definition is adjectival, describing the doctor who cannot sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually cannot get to sleep suffers from chronic wakefulness.

clue.text: With relocation, protects a witness

indicators.note: with relocation means the letters move to new positions

explanation.surface: A witness is guarded by being moved to a new home.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker who sees an event happen.

clue.text: Half of our capital allocated to country house, with an eye to the future

definitions.text: with an eye to the future

indicators.note: allocated to means the half is attached before the house
half of takes only the first three of the capital's six letters

parts.note: the Times is a London paper, so our capital is London
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: Half the city's funds are set aside for a manor in the shires.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range plans look far ahead, covering a distant span of time.

clue.text: Try wearing torn clothing

indicators.note: wearing means the word for torn has the try inside it like a garment around a body

parts.note: rent means torn, ripped
to aim is to try or endeavour

explanation.surface: An attempt to wear ripped garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothes or garments.

clue.text: Said to constrict Prometheus, for one

indicators.note: said means the word for constrict is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to constrict is to tighten

explanation.surface: Prometheus is said to have been bound tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Prometheus, chained to a rock in Greek myth, makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus was one of the giant pre-Olympian gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Flight simulator — it helps you run

definitions.meaning: a ground-based training device for pilots
a running shoe, or a coach for runners

explanation.definitionFit: A pilot's practice rig on the ground is a training device, and a sports shoe or coach supports an athlete.

clue.text: Dishes used to start the set

definitions.meaning: a matching set of plates and bowls, as in a dinner set
in tennis each point in a set begins with the server's first shot

explanation.definitionFit: A full set of matching tableware is a dinner service, and the opening tennis shot is the serve.

clue.text: Push to one side distress over having gained weight

indicators.note: having gained means the turned word takes the weight inside it
over in a down clue means the distress word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: woe is sorrow, distress
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A distressed person shoves aside someone who has put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push to one side' is the definition, not a description of the distress.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow is to shove someone aside with the arm.

clue.text: Teacher's first reprimand can make you sad

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Teacher's is taken

parts.note: an earful is a scolding

explanation.surface: A ticking-off from the teacher can leave a pupil upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone close to crying is unhappy, which is what sad means here.

clue.text: No end of chicken in China cooked like this?

indicators.note: no means a letter is taken out of the word for china

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate: china plate

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of chicken

explanation.surface: Chicken in a Chinese dish, prepared in a wok perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate). Remove N, the end of 'chicken', from FRIEND. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken cooked in hot oil, as in a stir-fry, has been prepared that way.

clue.text: Black eye doctor has to treat

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to treat something, as in handle it, is to use it

explanation.surface: An injured eye needs a physician's care.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUSE for a black eye is slang; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruised, swollen eye is called a mouse in old slang from its dark colour and shape.

clue.text: Don't put on rouge, say? It's detestable

indicators.note: say means the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: at roulette, not betting on red (rouge) means betting on black: bet noir

explanation.surface: Someone declines to wear make-up and calls it hateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rouge' looks like make-up but is the roulette colour red; its rival bet is on black, noir.
explanation.definitionFit: A bête noire is a pet hate, the thing one finds most loathsome.

clue.text: Watch or clock I heard

indicators.note: heard means the letter I is taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: A timepiece I listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch it or look at it closely, and to clock is slang for noticing.

clue.text: Sign agreement fellow backed

indicators.note: backed means the fellow's word is turned round

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man supported the signing of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head is a gesture that signals yes.

clue.text: Dominate game many go to see in London

definitions.text: many go to see in London

parts.note: to tower over is to dominate
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A popular game attracts crowds of spectators in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The bascule crossing beside the Tower of London is one of the city's best-known landmarks for visitors.
